mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced cost of capital.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% over 60-day horizons.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month consecutive rise in unemployment rate above 5.5% signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%) trigger Federal Reserve tightening, increasing real interest rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 2.5% over 5-day horizons.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105.0 indicates robust economic activity that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO remains above 105.0 over 60-day horizons.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) falling below 1,100,000 units signals weakening consumer demand for housing, which typically precedes reduced economic activity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST falls below 1100.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle expansion regimes (GDPC1 YoY > 2.5%) signal economic overheating that increases policy tightening risk, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 YoY exceeds 2.5% over 5-day horizons.
